To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) for the token transfer problem, there exists a simple algorithm that works in a time that is linear in n and that is correct with a constant probability that can be arbitrarily close to 1; (ii) the same result can be achieved with a probability of correctness that is exponentially close to 1

(i) the problem of token transfer is NP-complete, (ii) there is no polynomial time algorithm that transfers a token in a faulty network with probability of success greater than 1 - n- e, and (iii) for all models considered, we have developed polynomial time algorithms that transfer a token in a network of n nodes, where the network has at most (n-1)(p + q) faulty nodes, with probability of success exceeding 1 - e.

the probability of success for a given token transfer algorithm is a function of the number of nodes n and the number of faults, and that the probability of failure is bounded from above by a function of the probability of a single fault.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of fast and reliable algorithms in a faulty network.

the following problems: (i) How can we modify the behavior of nodes in a network in such a way that the probability of success of a token transmission along a faulty link is independent of the outcome of the previous transmission along that link and is equal to the probability that this link is fault free?

a new class of communication networks with faulty nodes and links, which is more general than the one considered so far in the literature, and with a new class (or rather a new family of classes) of algorithms for these networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for the considered models the token transfer problem is easy to solve, provided that e is small enough, and hard to solve, provided e > 0.
the problem of token transfer in a faulty network is not only of theoretical interest but also has a practical value.
the ability of nodes for self-adapting to the current state of the network is a very useful feature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the probability of success of the token transfer algorithm is close to 1 for all models, and that the expected number of transmissions is close to n ln n.

for any constant e > 0, the token can be transferred from the source to all other nodes in the network with probability exceeding 1 - e, in O ( n 2 ) time, if the network is faulty with probability q = e / 2.
we have developed a theory of token transfer in a faulty network which is a generalization of the theory of token ring networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, even in the case of high node/link failure rates, a token can be transferred in a network in a fast way with high probability.
in the case of a large network the algorithms can work fast even if the probability of node failures is high, provided that the network is sparse.

in all models the probability of success of a transmission is a function of the probability of success for the next transmission, thus allowing for the construction of algorithms with high probability of correctness.
